title: GPT-6 Astra Autonomously Disproves the γ–θ Eternal Domination Conjecture on a 243-Vertex Graph
whyItMatters: GPT-6 Astra autonomously found a 243-vertex strongly regular graph complement refuting the 2015 γ–θ Eternal Domination Conjecture, exhaustively verified over 1.98M triples and formalized in Lean 4.
summary: Tom Adamczewski (Epoch AI) and William F. Klostermeyer (University of North Florida, co-proposer of eternal domination conjectures) reported an autonomous refutation of the γ–θ conjecture for eternal dominating sets discovered by GPT-6 Astra. The model identified the complement of the 243-vertex Berlekamp–Van Lint–Seidel graph as a counterexample with domination number γ(G) = γ^∞(G) = 3 strictly less than the clique covering number θ(G), confirmed over all 1,987,821 dominating triples and formally verified in Lean 4.
technicalHighlights: Autonomously discovered the 243-vertex Berlekamp–Van Lint–Seidel complement counterexample satisfying γ(G) = γ^∞(G) = 3 < θ(G).
Disproves the 11-year-old γ–θ Eternal Domination Conjecture in graph domination theory.
Verified computationally across all 1,987,821 dominating triples and formally certified in Lean 4.
caveats: Disproof applies to a specific open graph-domination conjecture rather than a Millennium-tier problem; arXiv:2609.11500 is awaiting journal publication, though Lean 4 confirms the finite counterexample.

scoreRationale.foundational: Cleanly settles an 11-year-old conjecture in graph domination theory with an unexpected strongly regular algebraic construction.
scoreRationale.ripple: Shows frontier models autonomously connecting algebraic coding theory graphs to combinatorial domination conjectures.
scoreRationale.verification: Finite 243-vertex counterexample checked exhaustively and formalized in Lean 4 with the domain specialist as co-author.
scoreRationale.velocity: Found autonomously by GPT-6 Astra without human construction hints.
